mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month compresses discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy eases.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.0%, it signals labor market deterioration that triggers risk-off sentiment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when UNRATE > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.5%) and weak consumer credit demand (RSAFS < 500000) signals recession risk, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when both FEDFUNDS < 2.5% and RSAFS < 500000.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 109.0, it indicates supply chain disruptions that reduce corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when INDPRO < 109.0.

mechanism_narrative: A rising housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand and economic expansion, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as growth momentum accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when HOUST increases by at least 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 255.0, it signals persistent inflation that prompts aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL > 255.0.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE > 3.9%) and declining payroll employment (PAYEMS < 150000) signals labor market deterioration, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when both UNRATE > 3.9% and PAYEMS < 150000.

mechanism_narrative: In the context of slowing GDP growth (GDPC1 growth rate < 1.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days as recession expectations rise.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters when GDPC1 growth rate < 1.0%.
